title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 77
paragraphs: While Croesus had these plans in mind, the suburb of the city suddenly became full of serpents; and when they had appeared, the horses, leaving off feeding in their pastures, kept coming there and devouring them. When Croesus saw this he deemed it a portent, as indeed it was, and at once dispatched messengers to the dwelling of the Telmessians, who interpret omens. The messengers who were sent to consult arrived there and learned from the Telmessians what the portent meant to signify, but they did not succeed in reporting the answer back to Croesus, for before they could sail back to Sardis, Croesus had been taken prisoner. The Telmessians, however, gave their judgment thus: that an army speaking a foreign tongue was to be expected to invade Croesus’s land, and that when it came it would subdue the native inhabitants. For they said that the serpent was a child of the soil, while the horse was an enemy and a stranger. The men of Telmessus thus made their answer to Croesus after he had already been taken prisoner, not knowing as yet anything of what had happened to Sardis or to Croesus himself.
